title: Claude builds better when it interviews you first
hook: Claude builds better when it interviews you first.
summary: Metricool: scheduled Tue 27 Oct 18:00 IG + TikTok
body: Metricool: scheduled Tue 27 Oct 18:00 IG + TikTok
guide: Use an AI assistant to interview you into a clear set of requirements before it builds anything. You need ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code, and a rough idea of what you want to end up with.
1. Write the end goal in one or two sentences: what the finished thing does and who uses it.
1. Open ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code and ask it to interview you, one question at a time, working backwards from that goal.
1. Answer its questions about the architecture: what the pieces are, what talks to what, and in what order.
1. Ask it to question you on the cloud platform too (AWS, Google Cloud or Microsoft Azure) and why that one fits.
1. Say "I don't know" when you are unsure and ask it to explain the options in plain English, so you understand the structure.
1. Ask it to write everything up as one requirements document, then read it and correct anything wrong.
1. Start a fresh chat or session, paste in the finished requirements and ask the assistant to build from them.
Watch out: if you let the AI decide everything without understanding the structure, you cannot diagnose problems later, so only accept answers you can explain back.

```
You are a senior consultant helping me write requirements before anything is built. Do not write code yet.
My end goal: <one or two sentences on what the finished thing does and who uses it>.
What I already know: <tools, accounts, budget, deadline, or "nothing yet">.
Interview me one question at a time, working backwards from the end goal. Cover the architecture (the main pieces, what talks to what, in what order), which cloud platform to use (<AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, or undecided>) and why, what data is stored, who can access it, and what could go wrong. If I say I am unsure, explain the options in plain English and recommend one with your reasoning. Keep going until you have no open questions.
Then return a single requirements document with these headings: goal, users, architecture, cloud platform, data, risks, and a numbered build order. Flag any assumption you made so I can check it.
When I confirm the document, I will start a new session and ask you to build from it.
```
